name_en: the all-purpose soy sauce used in most Japanese kitchens
summary_ja: 国内のしょうゆ出荷量の約8割を占めるとされる、最も一般的な醤油。大豆と小麦をほぼ同量用いて造られ、赤みを帯びた色と強い香りを持つ。煮物からかけ用まで幅広く使われ、地域を問わず食卓の基本となっている。
summary_en: The most common soy sauce style, said to account for roughly 80% of national shipments. Made from roughly equal parts soybean and wheat, it carries a reddish color and a pronounced aroma, and serves as the everyday base seasoning nationwide.
source_publisher: しょうゆ情報センター（日本醤油協会）

name_en: the pale, aroma-forward soy sauce born in Tatsuno
summary_ja: 兵庫県たつの市（旧龍野）で寛文年間に考案されたと伝わる、色の淡い醤油。揖保川の軟水と播州平野の大豆・小麦、赤穂の塩に恵まれ、素材の色や出汁の風味を活かす関西の食文化とともに発達したとされる。
summary_en: A pale-colored soy sauce said to have been devised in the Kanbun era (1660s) in what is now Tatsuno, Hyogo. Soft water from the Ibo River and easy access to local soybeans, wheat, and Ako salt let it develop alongside a Kansai food culture that prizes ingredient color and dashi flavor.
source_publisher: 兵庫県

name_en: the thick, nearly all-soybean soy sauce of the Tokai region
summary_ja: 大豆を主原料に小麦をほとんど使わずに仕込む、とろみと濃厚な旨味が特徴の醤油。愛知・三重・岐阜の東海3県、なかでも知多半島の半田周辺が主産地とされ、豆味噌文化と地続きの醸造技術から生まれたとされる。
summary_en: A thick, deeply savory soy sauce brewed mainly from soybeans with little or no wheat. The Tokai region — Aichi, Mie, and Gifu, especially around Handa on the Chita Peninsula — is its main production area, growing out of the same brewing tradition as the region's soybean miso.
source_publisher: 愛知県味噌溜醤油工業協同組合

name_en: twice-brewed 'kanro' soy sauce from Yanai
summary_ja: できあがった生揚げ醤油に、もう一度麹を加えて仕込み直す濃厚な醤油。山口県柳井市の醸造家が江戸中期に生み出し藩主に献上したところ「甘露、甘露」と称えられ「甘露醤油」とも呼ばれるとされる。
summary_en: A rich soy sauce made by re-brewing already-finished raw soy sauce with a fresh batch of koji. Said to have been created in the mid-Edo period by a brewer in Yanai, Yamaguchi, who presented it to his lord — who reportedly praised it as 'kanro, kanro' (nectar, nectar), giving it the alternate name kanro shoyu.
source_publisher: 柳井市

name_en: the amber-pale, wheat-forward soy sauce of Mikawa
summary_ja: 小麦を主原料に大豆をわずかしか使わず仕込む、琥珀色に近い薄い色と強い甘みが特徴の醤油。愛知県碧南市が発祥の地とされ、白だしなど色を淡く仕上げたい料理の下味に使われる。
summary_en: Brewed mainly from wheat with only a small amount of soybean, this soy sauce is nearly amber in color and notably sweet. Hekinan, Aichi is said to be its birthplace, and it is prized for seasoning dishes — such as shiro-dashi — where a pale color matters.
source_title: 白しょうゆ発祥のまちで地元産有機白しょうゆ・みりんを使用した学校給食を提供
source_publisher: 碧南市

name_en: the sugar-rounded sweet soy sauce of Kyushu
summary_ja: 砂糖や甘味料を加えて仕込む、九州各地で好まれる甘口の醤油。江戸期の南蛮貿易で砂糖が早くから流通したことや、新鮮な魚を甘みで引き立てる食習慣が背景にあるとされ、刺身醤油として定着している。
summary_en: A sweetened soy sauce popular across Kyushu, made with added sugar or other sweeteners. Its roots are often traced to sugar arriving early via Edo-era trade with Portuguese and Dutch merchants, and to a local habit of using sweetness to complement very fresh raw fish — it remains the everyday sashimi soy sauce of the region.
source_title: 山口・九州地方における甘いしょうゆの歴史としょうゆと砂糖の関係
source_publisher: 農畜産業振興機構

name_en: 400 years of wooden-barrel brewing on Shodoshima
summary_ja: 約400年前に紀州湯浅の醸造技術が伝わったとされる、瀬戸内海・小豆島の醤油。温暖な気候と海運の便に恵まれ最盛期には島内に400軒の蔵があったとされ、現存する木桶仕込みの多くを今も小豆島産が占める。
summary_en: Soy sauce from Shodoshima in the Seto Inland Sea, whose brewing technique is said to have arrived from Yuasa in Kishu some 400 years ago. Mild climate and easy sea transport once supported some 400 breweries on the small island, and it still accounts for much of Japan's remaining wooden-barrel-aged soy sauce.
source_title: 小豆島町の特産品「本場の本物」小豆島桶(こが)仕込醤油
source_publisher: 小豆島町

name_en: soy sauce brewed where the Kuroshio meets the Tone River
summary_ja: 紀州の商人が江戸初期に興したとされる、関東を代表する醤油の産地。黒潮と親潮が交わる沖合の影響で夏冬の寒暖差が小さく高湿多湿な気候が、麹菌や酵母の働きに適していたとされ、江戸の食を支えた。
summary_en: One of Kanto's leading soy sauce production areas, said to have been founded by merchants from Kishu in the early Edo period. The mild, humid climate — shaped by the meeting of the Kuroshio and Oyashio currents offshore — is said to suit the koji mold and yeast used in brewing, and the town's output helped feed Edo.
source_publisher: 文化庁 日本遺産ポータルサイト

name_en: rice-koji miso, the nationwide standard
summary_ja: 米麹を使って仕込む味噌で、国内生産量の約8割を占めるとされる最も一般的な分類。信州味噌や江戸甘味噌など、産地ごとに塩分や熟成期間、色合いが異なる多様な地域味噌を含む大きな括りとなっている。
summary_en: Miso made with rice koji, said to account for roughly 80% of national miso production and by far the most common category. It is a broad umbrella covering many regional misos — from Shinshu to Edo amai — that differ widely in salt content, aging time, and color.
source_publisher: Wikipedia

name_en: barley-koji miso from Kyushu and the Inland Sea region
summary_ja: 麦麹を使って仕込む味噌で、九州や中国・四国地方など米作りが難しい土地で自家用に広まったとされる。米味噌より熟成が短く色が淡い傾向があり、麦の香ばしさと甘みを感じる素朴な味わいとされる。
summary_en: Miso made with barley koji, said to have spread as a home-brewed staple in Kyushu and the Chugoku-Shikoku region, where rice cultivation was historically harder. It tends to age faster and stay paler than rice miso, with a rustic sweetness and the toasty aroma of barley.
source_publisher: Wikipedia

name_en: soybean-only miso of the Tokai region
summary_ja: 大豆のみを原料に麹を造る、色濃く渋みのある味噌。愛知・三重・岐阜の東海3県を中心に生産されるとされ、八丁味噌に代表される長期熟成の力強い風味は、豆味噌文化圏に共通する特徴とされる。
summary_en: Miso made from soybeans alone, with a dark color and a slightly astringent depth. Production is centered on the Tokai region — Aichi, Mie, and Gifu — and its long, robust aging, typified by Hatcho miso, is a shared trait across the soybean-miso belt.
source_publisher: Wikipedia

name_en: Nagano's pale, tangy rice miso — half the nation's supply
summary_ja: 鎌倉時代に禅僧が製法を伝えたとの言い伝えを持つ、淡い黄色と軽い酸味が特徴の米味噌。長野県は出荷量・出荷額とも全国一とされ、国内で流通する味噌のおよそ半分を信州味噌が占めるとされる。
summary_en: A pale yellow, lightly tangy rice miso whose technique is said, by tradition, to have been brought by a Zen monk in the Kamakura period. Nagano leads Japan in both miso shipment volume and value, and Shinshu miso is said to make up roughly half of all miso distributed nationwide.
source_publisher: 長野県味噌工業協同組合連合会

name_en: the dark, long-aged miso Date Masamune stocked for war
summary_ja: 仙台藩祖・伊達政宗が城下に専用の味噌蔵を設けたのが始まりと伝わる、赤褐色で塩気の強い長期熟成味噌。朝鮮出兵の際に他藩の味噌が腐敗する中、仙台藩の味噌だけが変質しなかったとの逸話が伝わる。
summary_en: A reddish-brown, firmly salted, long-aged miso said to trace back to a dedicated miso storehouse built by Date Masamune, founding lord of the Sendai domain. A well-known anecdote holds that during a 16th-century overseas campaign, other domains' miso spoiled in the heat while Sendai's alone kept its quality.
source_publisher: 宮城県味噌醤油工業協同組合

name_en: Okazaki's deep-black, two-year soybean miso
summary_ja: 岡崎城から西へ八丁（約870メートル）の地区で造られてきたことに名が由来する豆味噌。大豆と塩水のみを原料に木桶と重石で2年以上熟成させ、黒に近い色と渋みを伴う濃厚な旨味を持つとされる。
summary_en: A soybean miso named for the district '8 cho' (about 870 meters) west of Okazaki Castle, where it has long been brewed. Made from only soybeans and brine, aged over two years in wooden barrels under stone weights, it develops a near-black color and a deep, slightly astringent umami.
source_publisher: 岡崎市観光協会

name_en: Kyoto's low-salt, sweet white miso for court cuisine
summary_ja: 京都所司代の依頼で宮中料理用に献上されたのが始まりと伝わる、塩分5%前後の低塩・甘口の白味噌。京都府味噌工業協同組合が原料や産地を定めて認定する呼称で、西京焼きなど京料理に欠かせない。
summary_en: A low-salt (around 5%), sweet white miso said to have originated when it was presented for court cuisine at the request of Kyoto's shogunal deputy. The name is a certified designation defined by the Kyoto Miso Industry Cooperative, governing ingredients and production area, and it is essential to Kyoto dishes such as saikyo-yaki.
source_title: 京みそ「西京味噌」について
source_publisher: 京都府味噌工業協同組合

name_en: Tokyo's short-aged, deep-brown sweet miso
summary_ja: 三河の豆味噌の旨味と京都白味噌の甘さを兼ね備えるよう考案されたと伝わる、麹を贅沢に使う甘口味噌。熟成期間が短く日持ちしない新鮮さが江戸っ子に好まれたとされ、東京都地域特産品にも認証されている。
summary_en: A sweet, koji-rich miso said to have been devised to combine the umami of Mikawa's soybean miso with the sweetness of Kyoto's white miso. Its short aging and short shelf life — meaning it had to be eaten fresh — reportedly suited Edo tastes, and it now carries Tokyo's regional specialty certification.
source_title: あぶまた 江戸甘味噌
source_publisher: 東京都地域特産品認証食品（Eマーク）

name_en: Niigata's floating-koji red miso
summary_ja: 精白した丸米を使うため麹粒が味噌の中に浮いて見えることから「浮麹味噌」とも呼ばれる、新潟県の赤色辛口味噌。上越・中越・下越・佐渡それぞれで気候風土に応じた作り方の違いがあるとされる。
summary_en: A red, savory miso from Niigata, also called 'ukikoji miso' (floating-koji miso) because its polished whole-grain rice koji appears to float within the paste. Its style is said to vary across Niigata's Joetsu, Chuetsu, Kaetsu, and Sado districts, each shaped by local climate.
source_publisher: 新潟県味噌醤油工業協同組合

name_en: Aomori's deep-red, long-aged cold-climate miso
summary_ja: 弘前藩が軍需備蓄として麹屋の営業を奨励したことから広まったとされる、色濃い赤色辛口の米味噌。足かけ3年におよぶ長期熟成と、寒冷な気候に合わせたやや高めの塩分が特徴とされる。
summary_en: A deep-red, savory rice miso said to have spread after the Hirosaki domain encouraged koji makers to operate as a form of military provisioning. It is typically aged for close to three years and carries a slightly higher salt content suited to the region's cold climate.
source_title: 公益社団法人 弘前観光コンベンション協会
source_publisher: 弘前観光コンベンション協会

name_en: the sweet, short-aged barley miso of Kyushu's table
summary_ja: 温暖な気候により熟成期間が短く、色が淡く甘口に仕上がるとされる九州の麦味噌。米作りより麦の裏作が根付いていた土地の事情から広まったとされ、塩分は全国平均より低めのものが多いとされる。
summary_en: A barley miso from Kyushu, said to age quickly and turn out pale and sweet thanks to the region's mild climate. It is said to have taken root where barley, grown as a second crop after rice, was more readily available than rice itself, and many versions carry lower salt than the national average.
source_publisher: Wikipedia

name_en: the miso once reserved for Tokushima's lord
summary_ja: 阿波藩主・蜂須賀家政の御膳に供されたことが名の由来と伝わる、麹を多く使うやや甘口の米味噌。藍の栽培の裏作として大豆が育てられていたことも背景にあるとされ、1966年に組合商標として登録された。
summary_en: A somewhat sweet rice miso, rich in koji, whose name is said to come from having been served at the table (gozen) of Hachisuka Iemasa, lord of the Awa domain. Soybeans grown as a rotation crop alongside the domain's indigo trade are cited as part of its background; it became a registered cooperative trademark in 1966.
source_title: Q 御膳みその由来は？
source_publisher: 徳島県味噌工業協同組合
